note: Written by an AI model from the 10-K figures in this folder. Covers 16 of the 38 companies. Review after running tools/build_data.py: the numbers quoted here are not updated automatically.

strengths: Huge cash generation: $136.1B of free cash flow in fiscal 2026, while spending only $9.0B on buildings and equipment.
Margins keep widening. Gross margin rose from 41.8% in fiscal 2021 to 48.8%, and net margin reached 27.6%.
Debt is steadily shrinking, from $124.7B in fiscal 2021 to $80.1B.
risks: Slow long-run growth: sales rose about 5.5% a year over five years and actually fell in fiscal 2023.
Debt ($80.1B) is still larger than cash and short-term investments ($56.7B). That figure leaves out long-term investments, so it understates Apple's cushion.
Shareholder equity is small ($112.1B) for a company this size, because most cash goes back to shareholders instead of staying on the balance sheet.

strengths: Exceptional profitability: a 46.8% operating margin and 40.3% net margin in fiscal 2026.
Fast, steady growth for its size. Sales nearly doubled from $168.1B to $331.8B in five years (about 14.6% a year) with no down year.
More cash than debt: $76.8B against $40.3B, and debt has fallen from $58.1B in fiscal 2021.
risks: Capital spending has exploded, from $20.6B in fiscal 2021 to $115.9B in fiscal 2026, most likely on data centres.
Free cash flow has drifted down for three years ($74.1B, $71.6B, $67.0B) even though operating cash flow hit a record $182.9B. The payoff from that spending is not yet visible in cash.
Gross margin slipped from 69.8% in fiscal 2024 to 67.9%, a sign that costs are growing faster than sales.

strengths: Strong growth at scale: sales rose from $182.5B to $402.8B in five years, about 17.2% a year.
Highly profitable, with a 32.8% net margin and $132.2B of net income in 2025.
A large cash pile: $126.8B in cash and short-term investments against $48.5B of debt.
risks: Capital spending quadrupled from $22.3B in 2020 to $91.4B in 2025, so free cash flow stayed flat near $73B while operating cash flow grew to $164.7B.
Debt more than tripled in a single year, from $14.2B to $48.5B.
Most of its revenue comes from advertising, which businesses tend to cut first when the economy slows.

strengths: Enormous scale that is still growing: $716.9B of sales in 2025, up about 13.2% a year over five years.
Profitability is improving quickly. Operating margin went from 2.4% in 2022 to 11.2%, and net income reached $77.7B.
More cash than debt: $123.0B against $68.9B.
risks: Capital spending of $131.8B swallowed almost all of the $139.5B in operating cash flow, leaving just $7.7B of free cash flow in 2025.
Free cash flow was negative in both 2021 and 2022, so its cash generation is far less dependable than its sales.
A 10.8% net margin is thin next to other large technology companies, which leaves less room for mistakes.

strengths: Very high margins: an 82.0% gross margin and a 41.4% operating margin in 2025.
Rapid growth, from $86.0B to $201.0B of sales in five years (about 18.5% a year).
Strong cash engine: $115.8B of operating cash flow, with $81.6B in cash against $58.7B of debt.
risks: Capital spending nearly doubled in one year, from $37.3B to $69.7B, pulling free cash flow down from $54.1B to $46.1B.
It went from no debt in 2021 to $58.7B in 2025.
Net income fell slightly in 2025 ($62.4B to $60.5B) despite 22% sales growth, and 2022 showed how fast profit can drop: net margin fell to 19.9% that year.

strengths: Extraordinary growth: sales went from $16.7B in fiscal 2021 to $215.9B in fiscal 2026, roughly 67% a year.
The highest margins in this set: a 55.6% net margin and $120.1B of net income.
It needs little capital. Free cash flow was $96.7B on just $6.0B of capital spending, and debt is only $8.5B against $49.7B of cash and short-term investments.
risks: The business is cyclical. In fiscal 2023 sales were flat and net income fell by more than half, from $9.8B to $4.4B.
Gross margin dipped from 75.0% to 71.1% in the latest year.
Growth this fast is rarely sustained, and it depends heavily on a small number of very large customers continuing to spend on AI data centres.

strengths: A very safe balance sheet: $44.1B in cash and short-term investments against only $6.6B of debt.
Sales tripled in five years, from $31.5B in 2020 to $94.8B in 2025.
Free cash flow has been positive every year since 2020, even while it built new factories.
risks: Growth has stalled. Sales went from $96.8B in 2023 to $97.7B and then down to $94.8B.
Profit has collapsed: net margin fell from 15.4% in 2022 to 4.0%, and net income from $12.6B to $3.8B.
Gross margin dropped from 25.6% to 18.0% over the same period, which suggests it is cutting prices to keep selling cars.

strengths: Margins are expanding fast: operating margin rose from 17.8% in 2022 to 29.5% in 2025.
It has turned into a real cash generator, going from roughly zero free cash flow in 2021 to $9.5B in 2025.
Consistent double-digit growth: sales rose about 12.6% a year over five years, to $45.2B.
risks: It carries more debt ($14.5B) than cash ($9.1B).
Cash flow has a weak history. Free cash flow was slightly negative as recently as 2021, because shows and films are paid for years before they earn money.
It has to keep spending heavily on new content to hold on to subscribers, so costs are hard to cut.

strengths: Profitability is recovering: operating margin climbed from 11.5% in fiscal 2021 to 19.3% in fiscal 2026.
Free cash flow grew from $2.0B to $10.6B over the same period.
It has been paying down debt, from $54.4B in fiscal 2021 to $44.5B.
risks: Debt is still heavy: $44.5B against only $6.7B of cash.
Bottom-line profit is uneven. Net income fell from $12.4B to $9.9B in fiscal 2026, and net margin was below 6% in every year from 2021 to 2024.
Capital spending has more than doubled since fiscal 2021, from $3.6B to $8.7B.

strengths: Gross margin near 43% shows the brand can still charge premium prices.
Low debt: $7.9B of borrowings is almost fully matched by $7.6B of cash and short-term investments.
It has stayed profitable and produced positive free cash flow every year, even during the downturn.
risks: Sales are going nowhere: $46.4B in fiscal 2026 is below the $51.2B of fiscal 2023, and five-year growth is under 1% a year.
Profit has roughly halved. Net margin fell from 12.9% in fiscal 2021 to 6.7%, and net income from $5.7B to $3.1B.
Free cash flow dropped from $6.6B in fiscal 2024 to $2.2B.

strengths: Very high margins for a consumer company: a 61.6% gross margin and a 27.3% net margin in 2025.
It needs little investment to run, with only $2.1B of capital spending on $47.9B of sales.
Steady growth from $33.0B in 2020 to $47.9B, although 2020 was a pandemic low point.
risks: Heavy debt: $45.4B against $13.9B of cash and short-term investments.
Profit is not fully turning into cash. Free cash flow was $5.3B in 2025 against $13.1B of net income, and operating cash flow is well below its 2023 level.
Growth has slowed to under 2% in the latest year ($47.1B to $47.9B).

strengths: Large and stable: $93.9B of sales with gross margin holding near 54% for years.
Dependable free cash flow, between $5.6B and $7.9B in each of the last six years.
Sales grew about 5.9% a year over five years.
risks: Debt of $49.2B is more than twice shareholder equity ($20.4B) and far above its $9.5B of cash.
Margins are slipping: operating margin fell from 14.0% to 12.2% in 2025 and net income from $9.6B to $8.2B.
Growth has slowed to about 2% a year ($91.9B to $93.9B).

strengths: The largest revenue here except Amazon: $706.4B in fiscal 2026, and it grew every single year.
Profit is rising faster than sales. Net income went from $13.5B to $21.9B in five years, and the 3.1% net margin is the best of the period.
Strong operating cash flow of $41.6B.
risks: Margins are razor thin. Keeping about $3 of every $100 in sales leaves little room for cost increases.
Capital spending rose from $10.3B to $26.6B, so free cash flow ($14.9B) is well below the $25.8B of fiscal 2021.
Debt of $44.8B is about four times its cash ($10.7B).

strengths: A cash-rich balance sheet: $21.3B in cash and short-term investments against $6.2B of debt.
Very consistent growth. Sales rose every year, about 9.1% a year over five years, to $303.2B.
Profit has nearly doubled, from $5.0B to $9.2B, with net margin inching up from 2.6% to 3.0%.
risks: Extremely thin margins: a 12.8% gross margin and a 3.0% net margin.
With so little profit per dollar of sales, a small drop in sales volume or a rise in costs would hit profit hard.
Capital spending is climbing, from $3.6B to $6.4B in five years.

strengths: A 46.1% operating margin, the result of collecting rent and fees from franchise owners instead of running most restaurants itself.
A 31.9% net margin in 2025.
Steady free cash flow of $5.5B to $7.3B a year since 2021.
risks: Very heavy debt: $41.5B against less than $1B of cash, equal to more than five years of free cash flow.
Negative shareholder equity (-$1.8B), meaning it owes more than the book value of what it owns.
Slow growth: sales rose only from $25.5B to $26.9B over the last two years.

strengths: Sales have grown every year, from $29.1B in fiscal 2021 to $37.9B in fiscal 2026.
Early signs of recovery: operating margin improved from 7.9% to 9.7% and net income from $1.9B to $2.5B in the latest year.
It reduced debt from $16.1B to $13.3B while free cash flow rose to $3.7B.
risks: Profitability is far below where it was. Operating margin was 16.8% in fiscal 2021 and is 9.7% now.
Negative shareholder equity (-$7.7B), and debt of $13.3B against $3.9B of cash.
Sales growth has slowed to about 2% a year.
